newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR GIVEN LITTLE HOPE OF SPRINGBOK RECALL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR GIVEN LITTLE HOPE OF SPRINGBOK RECALL.

text.p: New Springbok coach Carel du Plessis on Tuesday offered little hope of an early recall for axed former skipper Francois Pienaar.
"If the players in possession are not in the team when we take on the British Lions in June then they will only have themselves to blame," du Plessis told reporters.
"The squad that was put together last year will remain the nucleus of my team although injuries and the form of youngsters may mean some changes."

Du Plessis refused to rule out Pienaar completely -- as had predecessor Andre Markgraaff -- but his words were interpreted as a coded message that the World Cup winning skipper did not figure in his plans.
"I'm definitely not coming in and looking to make changes in the squad," he added.
"The players in the team are the form individuals. They have done well for the team."
Du Plessis said the selectors would view tapes of Pienaar in action for his new English club Saracens but they did not initially forsee selecting players from outside South Africa.
That would also thwart any prospect of an early recall for former Springbok flyhalf Joel Stransky, now playing in England for Leicester or Bath's South African lock Steve Atherton.
Du Plessis was appointed coach on Tuesday following Markgraaff's resignation after the publication of a secret tape recording in which he had made racist insults against black sports administrators.
Du Plessis was part of the Springbok management team which steered South Africa to a five-test clean sweep of victories on their end of season tour of Argentina, France and Wales.
His first match in charge in a year of 13 internationals will be against Tonga in Cape Town, provisionally scheduled for June 10.
